questions.q: Which two questions does an inspectional read aim to answer?
a: What the book is about and what kind of book it is
Who the author is and when the book was written
Whether the book is enjoyable and worth recommending
How long it will take and how many pages it has
questions.why: Lesson 1 says inspectional reading establishes the subject and the category of the book.

questions.q: According to the summary, where should you save time on books?
a: In deciding which books to read in the first place
By speed reading every page as quickly as possible
By skipping introductions and conclusions
By reading only the final chapter of each book
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues the real time saving comes from choosing what to read, not from reading faster.

questions.q: What does the summary advise while reading a book cover to cover?
a: Keep going without stopping to look things up
Pause to research every unfamiliar reference
Take detailed notes on the content of each page
Read the chapters in reverse order
questions.why: Lesson 1 says looking things up slows you down; grasp the whole text first and dig deeper later.

questions.q: What should you identify first when analyzing a book?
a: The author's aim in writing it
The number of chapters it contains
The reputation of its publisher
The age of the intended reader
questions.why: Lesson 2 says asking why the author wrote the book helps you categorize it and follow its theme.

questions.q: Which two questions should you ask after finishing a book?
a: Is this true, and so what?
Who else read it, and why?
Was it long, and was it fun?
What did it cost, and was it worth it?
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends checking the book's logic first, then asking whether its message matters.
